subtopics.title: The purpose and nature of business activity

outcomes.text: Understand scarcity, needs, wants, opportunity cost, specialisation, business purposes, and how businesses increase added value.

subtopics.title: Economic sectors in terms of primary, secondary and tertiary sectors

outcomes.text: Classify businesses by economic sector and explain why sector importance changes between developed and developing economies.
Identify successful entrepreneur characteristics, business-plan contents and how governments support start-ups.

subtopics.title: The main features of different forms of business organisation

outcomes.text: Compare business organisation forms, liability, ownership and risk, and recommend a suitable structure for a situation.

subtopics.title: Businesses can have several objectives and the importance of them can change

outcomes.text: Explain why objectives matter, how they change, and compare profit, survival, growth, market-share and social-enterprise objectives.

subtopics.title: The importance of a well-motivated workforce

outcomes.text: Explain workforce motivation, human needs, motivational theories and benefits such as higher productivity and lower absenteeism.

subtopics.title: Draw, interpret and understand simple organisational charts

outcomes.text: Interpret organisational charts, including hierarchy, span of control and command chains, and explain organisational roles.

topics.title: 2.3 Recruitment, selection and training of employees

outcomes.text: Explain recruitment and selection methods, internal and external recruitment, employment types, and recommend candidates.

subtopics.title: Why effective communication is important and the methods used to achieve it

outcomes.text: Explain communication’s business importance, compare communication methods and recommend suitable choices.
Explain how marketing identifies and satisfies customer needs, builds relationships and maintains loyalty.

subtopics.title: The role of market research and methods used

outcomes.text: Explain market research, primary and secondary methods, sampling, accuracy factors and their benefits and limitations.
Understand product development, branding, packaging, product life cycles, extension strategies and related marketing decisions.

subtopics.title: Justify marketing strategies appropriate to a given situation

outcomes.text: Evaluate marketing-mix elements and recommend a suitable strategy for influencing consumer decisions.
Explain production, productivity, efficiency, inventories and lean production, including just-in-time and Kaizen.

topics.title: 4.2 Costs, scale of production and break-even analysis

outcomes.text: Classify fixed, variable, average and total costs and use cost data for simple production decisions.

subtopics.title: Why quality is important and how quality production might be achieved

outcomes.text: Explain quality’s importance and distinguish between quality control and quality assurance.

subtopics.title: The main factors influencing the location and relocation decisions of a business

outcomes.text: Assess location factors for manufacturing and services, including countries and legal controls, then recommend a location.
Explain why businesses need finance, including start-up capital, expansion and working capital.
Identify internal and external finance sources, with examples.
Explain why businesses need finance, distinguish internal, external, short-term and long-term sources, and justify suitable financing choices in different circumstances.
Explain why cash is important to a business.
Explain the meaning and importance of working capital.
Explain the importance of cash, prepare and interpret simple cash-flow forecasts, address short-term cash shortages, and understand working capital.
Explain how a business makes profit.
Identify the main features of an income statement, including revenue, costs, gross profit and retained profit.
Explain profit and its importance, distinguish profit from cash, identify income statement components, and use profit calculations for decisions.
Classify assets and liabilities using appropriate examples.
Interpret a simple statement of financial position and deduce how activities are financed and what assets are owned.
Classify assets and liabilities, then interpret a simple statement of financial position to assess financing, ownership and inventory sales.
Explain the meaning and importance of profitability.
Explain the meaning and importance of liquidity.
Calculate and interpret gross profit margin.
Explain the information needs of different accounts users and ratio analysis.
Understand profitability and liquidity, calculate and analyse key ratios, and use accounts to support lending and investment decisions.
Identify the main business-cycle stages: growth, boom, recession and slump.
Identify government economic objectives, such as increasing GDP.
Understand business-cycle stages, economic indicators, government objectives, taxation, spending and interest rates, and how businesses respond to economic changes.

subtopics.title: Environmental concerns and ethical issues as both opportunities and constraints for businesses

outcomes.text: Explain how business activity can affect the environment, including through global warming.
Understand environmental impacts, externalities, sustainability, regulation, pressure groups and ethical dilemmas, and how businesses respond to environmental and ethical pressures.
Explain globalisation and the reasons it occurs.
Explain benefits to businesses of becoming multinational and impacts on stakeholders.
Explain depreciation and appreciation of an exchange rate.
